explain.say: On 1 October 1949, standing on the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China. It ended more than a century of foreign invasions and civil wars. Look at the timeline, from the empire's fall in 1911 to this day. Who would have predicted it twenty years earlier?

explain.say: Here is the puzzle. Look at the sizes, approximate. In 1946 Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists had about 4.3 million soldiers and American support; the Communists had about 1.2 million. By 1949 the Communist army had grown to about 4 million and won. So the stronger side lost. What could make soldiers and villages switch sides?

See the reasons. In the areas they ran, the Communists gave landlords' land to poor peasants, winning millions of supporters. Eight years of war with Japan exhausted the Nationalists, and inflation and corruption ruined trust in their cities. The Communist army was disciplined and skilled at guerrilla war. Which reason would matter most to a farming family?

explain.say: Now the map. In 1948 and 1949 Communist armies won huge battles in Manchuria and the north, took Beijing, crossed the Yangtze in April 1949 and captured the Nationalist capital, Nanjing. Chiang retreated to Taiwan in December. Since then two governments have claimed to be China. Why might an island be easier to defend?

draw.label: From civil war to two Chinas

explain.say: Now the debate. Chalmers Johnson argued resistance to Japan created peasant nationalism; Mark Selden stressed land reform and mass mobilisation. Both matter. The new state also brought great suffering, including the famine of the Great Leap Forward in which tens of millions died. Great work. Challenge: weigh Nationalist weakness against Communist strength.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: War with Japan and land reform worked together.

faq.q: Why did the Communists win the Chinese Civil War?
faq.a: Land reform won peasant support, eight years of war with Japan weakened the Nationalists, inflation and corruption destroyed trust in Chiang's government, and the Communist army was disciplined and well led. Captured Japanese arms in Manchuria also helped.

A retreat of about 10,000 kilometres by Communist forces from 1934 to 1935, fleeing Nationalist encirclement in the south to a new base around Yan'an in the north-west. Most who set out died or left, but it made Mao the party's leader and a lasting legend.
asks: Where did the Long March go?

faq.q: Why did the Nationalists go to Taiwan?
faq.a: After losing the main battles of 1948 and 1949, Chiang Kai-shek's government retreated to the island of Taiwan in December 1949, protected by the sea and later by the US Navy. It continued as the Republic of China.
asks: What is the Republic of China?

faq.a: Leader of the Nationalist Party, the Guomindang, who ruled much of China from 1928, fought both the Communists and Japan, and governed Taiwan from 1949 until his death in 1975.

faq.q: How did the war with Japan affect the civil war?
faq.a: From 1937 Japan's invasion drained Nationalist armies and finances, while the Communists expanded behind Japanese lines, built rural bases and presented themselves as patriotic resisters. Chalmers Johnson called this peasant nationalism.

facts: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China on 1 October 1949.
The Chinese Communist Party was founded in Shanghai in 1921.
The Nationalist government moved to Taiwan in December 1949.

quiz.say: The Communist army grew from about 1.2 million in 1946 to about 4 million in 1949. About how many times bigger is that?
quiz.why: 4 divided by 1.2 is about 3.3, so roughly three times bigger.

quiz.say: Which policy won the Communists the most peasant support?
quiz.show: Peasants were won over mainly by…
quiz.why: Taking land from landlords and giving it to poor peasants built mass support.

wrong.2: Shanghai was a Nationalist-held city until 1949.
